title: Happy Number Cycle Check
description:
Starting with a positive integer `n`, repeatedly replace the number by the sum of the squares of its base-10 digits. This defines an implicit singly linked list of states where each integer points to its digit-square sum.

Return `true` if this sequence eventually reaches `1` (making `n` a happy number), or `false` if it enters a cycle that never includes `1`. Solve in `O(1)` extra space using Floyd's fast and slow pointers.
hints: Treat the transition `next(x) = sum of squares of digits of x` as following a `.next` pointer in an implicit linked list.
Advance `slow = next(slow)` by one step and `fast = next(next(fast))` by two steps; the loop terminates when `fast == 1` (happy) or `slow == fast` (cycle).

examples.explanation: 2 -> 4 -> 16 -> 37 -> 58 -> 89 -> 145 -> 42 -> 20 -> 4 enters a cycle without 1, so return false.
